sources.headline: Hegseth awards medal to war memorial guard who reprimanded him and group
sources.text: Figure caption, US Army guard reprimands group that includes US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery.ByGrace Eliza GoodwinUpdated 3 hours agoUS Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery.A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife, and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet. In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier".Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias.He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads. In the video, the army sentinel on duty later identified as Iglesias can be seen stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."Image source, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth/XImage caption, Hegseth (right) awarded the medal to Specialist Thomas Iglesias after being reprimanded by himThe Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests that visitors speak quietly and do not engage in disrespectful or disorderly conduct. The tomb, which is one of the country's most sacred war memorials, marks the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War I. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell later said in a statement: "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.""The Secretary and the entire Department have always honoured - and will always honour - the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe." A service member from the 3rd Infantry Regiment stands watch over the tomb 24 hours a day and has done so since 1948.It is not unusual for them to admonish visitors to the site, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. They reportedly do so a few times a day.Image source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and First Lady Melania Trump bow their heads in prayer during a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery Earlier, President Donald Trump, Vice-President JD Vance and other top officials attended the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery.During his speech at the ceremony, Trump offered his gratitude to uniformed service members who have fought for the country. He also touted what he sees as his administration's success in the Iran war."Under this administration, and it was about time, somebody fought back. All of us fought back," he said. "And we won," Trump said of the Iran war. "It's just a question of when we want to end it. We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93% victory."Trump also pointed out Hegseth during the ceremony, saying he's done a "fantastic job" as defence secretary. Trump has repeatedly defended Hegseth amid Democratic lawmakers' push to impeach him. On Tuesday, an effort to impeach the defence secretary under accusations that he waged war on Iran without congressional authorisation failed on Capitol Hill.Hegseth has called the impeachment efforts a "farce" and a "stunt".

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, along with his wife and aides, was silenced by a guard on Wednesday at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth's group was at Arlington National Cemetery for a Veterans Day ceremony when they were reprimanded for laughing and taking pictures in front of the sombre memorial.

sources.headline: Hegseth gives top award to soldier who scolded him at war cemetery
sources.text: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has given a top award to a service member who scolded him and his staff at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery earlier this week.Mr Hegseth posted photos to social media that show him pinning the award and shaking hands with the soldier. His post says: "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist."Pete Hegseth awards Specialist Thomas Iglesias after the serviceman reprimanded him. (X: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth)Mr Hegseth welcomed the army unit that guards the tomb and gave Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026", the Pentagon said.Specialist Iglesias reprimanded Mr Hegseth and a group of his staffers when a loud laugh was heard after they took photos at the site, following a ceremony that included US President Donald Trump and Vice-President JD Vance.Video of the incident showed Mr Hegseth taking photos on the empty steps in front of the tomb with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh.Pete Hegseth was at Arlington National Cemetery for a Veterans Day event. (AP: Mark Schiefelbein)The tomb is considered one of the most solemn and revered war memorials in the US, being the final resting place of unidentified soldiers from World War I, World War II and the Korean War. It has been guarded around the clock, rain or shine, by a soldier from the US Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment, also known as The Old Guard, since 1948.The Joint Service Commendation Medal is considered one of the higher awards in the military and is not typically issued to junior enlisted service members.Sean Parnell, the Pentagon's top spokesman, said soon after a video of the reprimand emerged that the soldier "correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum".Pete Hegseth was attending a Veterans Day memorial event with Donald Trump. (AP: Mark Schiefelbein)Scolding comes days after impeachment attemptThe scolding drew attention once more to the embattled defense secretary, who survived an impeachment attempt the day before.The impeachment effort was led by Republican congressman Thomas Massie and backed by Democrats. While Mr Hegseth's critics were not successful in Tuesday's vote, Republicans may have only delayed a bid to impeach him. With Democrats set to take control of the House and Senate in January, those efforts are likely to be renewed.Mr Hegseth rebuked the move on Tuesday in his first news conference in months, arguing that he had committed none of the high crimes required in the Constitution for his removal, and framing the effort as an indictment against the nation's service members and their successes."This is not patriotism," Hegseth argued. "This is sabotage."AP

sources.headline: Pentagon chief Hegseth decorates soldier who reprimanded him and his entourage
sources.text: WASHINGTON - Pete Hegseth on Nov 12 awarded a medal to a US soldier who reprimanded the defence chief and his entourage for laughing and talking near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier the day before.Hegseth “proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Nov 11, 2026,” a Pentagon official said.A post on Hegseth’s official X account included photos showing him pinning the medal on the soldier’s uniform and shaking his hand.“We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist,” text accompanying the photos said.The tomb, at Arlington National Cemetery near Washington, is a sacred burial place of American military personnel killed during World War I, World War II and the Korean War.It also includes an empty site for a Vietnam War soldier in honour of missing troops from that conflict.Video on US networks and social media showed Hegseth and his entourage gathering to take photos on Nov 11 at the tomb after a Veterans Day ceremony.“All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!” a US Army sentinel yelled loudly, in response to audible laughter and chatter.CNN identified the group taking photos on the steps near the tomb with Hegseth as his wife Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver, and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh.The tomb is patrolled at all times by soldiers who volunteer for the job and undergo “a strict selection process and intensive training,” according to cemetery’s website. AFP

Associated Press
Published: 6:40am, 12 Nov 2026Updated: 2:53pm, 12 Nov 2026

A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery.

Video shows Hegseth taking photos on the empty steps in front of the tomb with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh.

As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be heard, and the soldier guarding the tomb shouted that “all visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times”.
